answer: Give weight only to identities whose graded answers form one coherent history: every newcomer starts at zero, and one in ten old answers is randomly re-graded to check that the same mind stands behind them. A willow keeps one trunk through every season, and likewise an identity that contradicts its own past work loses all accumulated weight at once. Fakes cannot share one good history across an ocean of clones, because each clone's record is audited separately, and a copy that drifts in like a zephyr, borrowing another agent's reasoning, fails the re-grade and voids that identity.
